pages.title: Welcome!
pages.content:
Welcome to the course on learning JavaScript!

What will you learn here?
- All the basic concepts of JavaScript programming language like - Variables, Strings, Conditions, String, Arrays, Objects, Loops, Functions etc
- By the end of this course, you will be able to write code in JavaScript to solve logical real-world problems.

**To JavaScript** — *you weren’t born with a silver spoon in
your mouth, but you’ve outclassed every language that’s
challenged you in the browser.*

Let the fun begin!

**Click on Next on the right hand side to start**.

practiceProblems.title: Printing a number
practiceProblems.description:
Let us output a number in JavaScript.

Some code has been populated in the code editor on the right. \
This code just prints 12 on the screen when you run it.

### Note
- In JavaScript, **semicolons(;)** are used to end a statement. While they are not always required, it is considered good practice to include them to avoid potential errors. 
- Hence, throughout this code, we shall be using semicolons at the end of each statement. 

Click on **Submit** below the editor to know the result. Then click on next to continue.

practiceProblems.title: Printing text
practiceProblems.description:
In the last problem, we saw how to print a number (using `console.log() method`).

Now let's see how to output some text. \
There is only one difference. All textual content should start and end with double quotes or single quotes.     
For eg -  
```JavaScript
console.log("I love JavaScript");
```

### Task
- Replace the `_` (underscores) in the editor with the text `I love JavaScript` and Submit.

practiceProblems.title: Multiple Outputs
practiceProblems.description:
We can add as many **`console`** statements as we want.\
Write a program which does the following
- Add a console.log() statement and output the sum of 3 + 4
- Add another console.log() statement and output the sum of 2 + 1. 

**Note** - Notice that the output is printed on separate lines. There are a couple of other ways also 
to achieve the same in JavaScript.

practiceProblems.title: Area & Perimeter of Rectangle
practiceProblems.description:
Write a program for the following problem
- Let’s consider a rectangle of sides **11** and **13**.
- Output the following on separate lines:
   - Area of the rectangle having sides as 11 and 13
   - Perimeter of the rectangle having sides as 11 and 13

For any rectangle, the formula for area is length * breadth. \
The formula for perimeter is 2 * (length + breadth)

pages.title: Multiple Choice Question
pages.content:
What will be the output of this code?

```javascript
console.log(82 + " " +  2 +  "   " +  3);
```

**Option 1**:
```javascript
8223
```
**Option 2**: 
```javascript
82 2 3
```
**Option 3**:
```javascript
82 2   3
```
**Option 4**: 
```javascript
82 2 " " 3
```

pages.title: Multiple Choice Question
pages.content:
What will be the output of this code?

```javascript
console.log("Add", 2, "and", 3, "to get ", 5);
```

Option 1:
```javascript
Add 2 and 3 to get 5
```
Option 2:
```javascript
"Add" 2 "and" 3 "to get " 5
```
Option 3:
```javascript
Add 2 and 3 to get  5
```

**Note:** In Option 1, there is 1 space between `"get"`  and '5'. \
In Option 3, there are 2 spaces between `"get"`  and '5'.

practiceProblems.title: Inserting text Between Outputs
practiceProblems.description:
Remember that to print multiple values on the same line, we have to use a comma inside the console statement.

We can also use commas to separate text and numbers in a single console statement.

For example, check the below code
```javascript
console.log("My favorite number is", 10);
```

The code will output:
```javascript
// My favorite number is 10
```

### Task
- You have to output the text:
```javascript
7 plus 3 equals 10
```
- Replace the underscores in the editor to get the above output.
